title: Sprint 9 - Set Operations & Advanced Schema
description: Complete all MongoDB queries in this sprint.

tickets.title: Find Alice's Tasks via Subquery
tickets.description:
Find all task titles for the user 'alice_dev' without using a lookup/join, but instead by querying the user collection inline.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
SELECT title FROM todos 
WHERE user_id = (
    SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'alice_dev'
);
```
tasks: Find all task titles for the user 'alice_dev' without using a lookup/join, but instead by querying the user collection inline.
learning_objectives: Use nested queries in place of joins.
common_mistakes: Doing a $lookup join instead of querying inline.
hints: Resolve the user ID using db.users.findOne first, then pass it as user_id filter.

scoring_rules.system_query: db.todos.find({ user_id: db.users.findOne({ username: "alice_dev" })._id }, { title: 1, _id: 0 }).sort({ title: 1 })

tickets.title: User Task Counts (CTE)
tickets.description:
Calculate the total tasks per user_id, returning the fields `user_id` and `total_tasks`.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
WITH user_counts AS (
    SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as total_tasks 
    FROM todos 
    GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT * FROM user_counts;
```
tasks: Calculate the total tasks per user_id, returning the fields `user_id` and `total_tasks`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to project user_id from the group _id key.
hints: Group by _id: "$user_id" and then project user_id from the _id.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql

```
tasks: Create an index called `idx_todos_status` on the `status` field of the `todos` collection.

common_mistakes: Creating the index without naming it.

tickets.title: Inspect Indexed Columns
tickets.description:
Inspect the index `idx_todos_status` to see its key definitions. Note: Since `db.todos.getIndexes()` returns a standard JavaScript array of index definitions (not a MongoDB cursor), we isolate the index named `"idx_todos_status"` using JavaScript's built-in `.filter()` function in the shell.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
PRAGMA index_info('idx_todos_status');
```
tasks: Inspect the index `idx_todos_status` to see its key definitions. Note: Since `db.todos.getIndexes()` returns a standard JavaScript array of index definitions (not a MongoDB cursor), we isolate the index named `"idx_todos_status"` using JavaScript's built-in `.filter()` function in the shell.
common_mistakes: Trying to lookup index_info via system.indexes, or forgetting that getIndexes() returns a JS array.
hints: Use JavaScript array .filter() on the getIndexes() list.

tickets.title: Altering Table Schema
tickets.description:
The product team wants to track when a task was last updated. Since MongoDB collections are schemaless, there is no direct schema alteration command (like SQL's ALTER TABLE). Instead, we simulate adding a new field `updated_at` (current date) to the schema by updating all existing documents in the `todos` collection using `updateMany()`.

### SQL Equivalent
```sql
ALTER TABLE todos ADD COLUMN updated_at DATE;
```
tasks: The product team wants to track when a task was last updated. Since MongoDB collections are schemaless, there is no direct schema alteration command (like SQL's ALTER TABLE). Instead, we simulate adding a new field `updated_at` (current date) to the schema by updating all existing documents in the `todos` collection using `updateMany()`.
